latin.571: §. XVI. Berengarii, circa finem Seculi XI. piè demortui vestigia, docendo de S. Cœna, legit Asceticorum Scriptorum suo tempore facilè Princeps BERNHARDUS ABBAS CLARÆVALLENSIS sub ipsum ferè SECULI XIImi INITIUM, quo de testes sunt amplissimæ, binæ ejus Conciones indubitatò illi tribuendæ, altera de purificatione Mariæ, de S. Martino altera conscripta habitaque. In priori legeris, quòd Christi corpus in Mysterio (Cœnæ) cibus mentis sit, non ventris, proinde corporaliter non manducetur, sicut enim cibus est, ita & comedi intelligitur. In posteriori verò: Quod usque hodie eadem caro Christi, nobis, sed spiritualiter utique, non corporaliter exhibeatur.
latin.572: Quô duplici effatô nervosissimâ omnem de corpore Christi in S. Cœna veritatem perorat, (1) faciendo istud cibum mentis eóque cibum Spiritualem, quodque idcirco (2) non corporaliter, sed spiritualiter præsens sit ac exhibeatur. Denique, (3.) Spiritualiter exhibitum, spiritualiter etiam proptereà manducetur, quia naturam rationemque cibi insequatur natura & ratio manducationis; Eóque, uti cibus corporalis, corporaliter assumtus, in corporis usum, ita cibus spiritualis, spiritualiter seu fide acceptus, in usum Spiritus, seu Animæ fidelis, i. e. in augmentum ac stabilimentum fidei communionisque cum Christo concedat. Confer Sermonem Bernhardi de S. Cœna in Caput VI. Johannis versum 56. 563.
latin.573: Progressu Seculi, PETRUS DE BRUIS & Henricus quidam Monachus, in variis Galliæ partibus, pauloque post, PETRUS WALDUS Civis Lugdunensis, cum quodam Arnoldo socio, in Civitatibus Lugdunensi & Albigensi, veram, etiam de S. Cœna doctrinam, longè latèque prædicando disseminarunt, Sequacibus, ab istorum partim, partim à civitatum, in quibus illi docuêre, nominibus, Petro-Bruisiani, Arnoldistæ, Waldenses seu Waldenses, Pauperes de Lugduno, Albienses seu Albigenses appellatis, innumerisque à Pontificum Rom. assentatoribus, gravatis calumniis, quas tamen Nostrates efficacissimè toties quoties absterserunt ac diluerunt, interque hos doctissimus Armachanus, Libro sæpiùs citato de Success. ac Stat. Eccles. Occidentalium.
latin.574: Sententia Waldensium istius temporis de S. Eucharistia, QUA VERBORUM INSTITUTIONIS CHRISTI INTERPRETATIONEM genuinam, vel ex ipsorum Pontificiorum relatione, cognoscere datur, puta tùm illius ætatis Auctoris Petri Lombardi, Sententiarum Lib. 4. Distinct. 10. Quæst. I. scribentis: Sunt quidam (Waldenses notat Auctor) asserentes in altari non esse corpus Christi vel sanguinem (intellige corporaliter præsentia); Sed ita Christum dixisse, hoc est Corpus meum, sicut Apostolus dixit, Petra autem erat Christus: dicunt ibi esse corpus Christi tantùm in Sacramento, h. e. in Signo; tum Junioris Rainerii, Sectam Waldensium omnibus aliis diuturniorem seu antiquiorem facientis, & ad tempora vel Sylvestri, vel ipsorum Apostolorum, referentis, quando in Summ. de Catharis & Leonistis refert, credidisse Waldenses, panem benedictum, in Figura quadam, dici corpus Christi, sicut dicitur, petra autem erat Christus.
latin.575: QUA ASSERTAM VERAM CORPORIS CHRISTI IN S. CŒNA PRÆSENTIAM, ex Confessione eorum antiquiori, circa annum 1200. scripta, apud Hovedenum in Annalibus fol. 319. constat, in qua dicunt: Credimus, quod non salvatur, qui non manducat corpus Christi,
latin.576: etiam Transsubstantiationis portentosum vocabulum, teste Rainerio, sensu tamen Spirituali, haud defugientes, quando docent, Transsubstantiationem non fieri in manu conficientis, sed in ore dignè sumentis: Non, quasi panem in ore dignè sumentium in substantiam corporis Christi converti putassent, sed quod Sacramentum arbitrati sint etiam suo modo in ore dignè sumentium non tantum significativum (quale & in ore impiorum) sed & exhibitivum corporis & sanguinis Domini esse, quatenus sumtis, ore corporis fidelium, symbolis, simul & res significata, corpus & sanguis Christi, gustu fidei percipiuntur.

pass_a.571: §. XVI. The footsteps of Berengar, piously deceased around the end of the XIth Age, in teaching concerning the Sacred Supper, BERNARD ABBOT OF CLAIRVAUX, easily Prince of Ascetic Writers in his time, followed near the very BEGINNING OF THE XIIth AGE — of which the witnesses are two most ample Sermons undoubtedly attributed to him, one On the Purification of Mary, the other On S. Martin, written and delivered. In the former you will read that Christ’s body in the Mystery (of the Supper) is food of the mind, not of the belly, and therefore is not eaten corporally; for as it is food, so also it is understood to be eaten. But in the latter: That even to this day the same flesh of Christ is exhibited to us, but spiritually indeed, not corporally.
pass_a.572: By which double utterance most sinewy he perorates the whole truth concerning Christ’s body in the Sacred Supper, (1) by making it food of the mind and therefore Spiritual food, and therefore (2) that it is present and exhibited not corporally but spiritually. Finally, (3.) what is Spiritually exhibited is therefore also eaten spiritually, because the nature and reason of eating follows the nature and reason of the food; And so, as corporal food taken corporally goes to the use of the body, so spiritual food received spiritually or by faith goes to the use of the Spirit, or of the faithful Soul — i.e. to the increase and establishment of faith and of communion with Christ. Compare Bernard’s Sermon on the Sacred Supper on John ch. 6 verse 56 (563).
pass_a.573: As the Age progressed, PETER DE BRUIS and a certain Henry the Monk, in various parts of Gaul, and a little later PETER WALDO Citizen of Lyons, with a certain Arnold as companion, in the Cities of Lyons and Albi, disseminated far and wide by preaching the true doctrine even concerning the Sacred Supper — their Followers called from partly their names, partly the cities in which they taught: Petrobrusians, Arnoldists, Waldenses, Poor of Lyons, Albigenses — weighed down by innumerable calumnies from Roman Pontiffs’ flatterers, which yet Our men most effectively wiped away and washed off as often as they arose, and among these the most learned Armachanus in the often-cited Book on the Succession and State of the Western Churches.
pass_a.574: The sentence of the Waldenses of that time concerning the Sacred Eucharist, BY WHICH the genuine INTERPRETATION OF CHRIST’S INSTITUTION WORDS is given to be known even from the Pontificals’ own report — namely both from Peter Lombard, Author of that age, Sentences Book 4 Dist. 10 Qu. I, writing: There are some (the Author notes Waldenses) asserting that on the altar there is not the body or blood of Christ (understand: corporally present); But that Christ said This is my Body as the Apostle said And the Rock was Christ: they say Christ’s body is there only in the Sacrament, i.e. in the Sign; and from the younger Rainerius, making the Waldensian Sect more long-lasting or older than all others and referring it to the times of Sylvester or even of the Apostles themselves, when in the Summa on Cathars and Leonists he reports that the Waldenses believed the blessed bread is called Christ’s body in a certain Figure, as it is said And the rock was Christ.
pass_a.575: BY WHICH the ASSERTED TRUE PRESENCE OF CHRIST’S BODY IN THE SACRED SUPPER is clear from their more ancient Confession written around the year 1200, in Hoveden’s Annals fol. 319, in which they say: We believe that he is not saved who does not eat the body of Christ,
pass_a.576: even the monstrous vocabulary of Transubstantiation, Rainerius witnessing, they by no means flee — yet in a Spiritual sense — when they teach that Transubstantiation does not happen in the hand of the one confecting but in the mouth of the one worthily taking: Not as if they thought bread in the mouth of the worthily taking is converted into the substance of Christ’s body, but that they judged the Sacrament also in its own mode in the mouth of the worthily taking to be not only significative (as also in the mouth of the impious) but also exhibitive of the Lord’s body and blood, inasmuch as, the symbols taken by the faithful’s bodily mouth, at the same time also the thing signified — the body and blood of Christ — is perceived by the taste of faith.

571: §.XVI: near the opening of the XIIth age, BERNARD OF CLAIRVAUX — then prince of ascetic writers — walks Berengar’s footsteps on the Sacred Supper.
Two sermons (Purification of Mary; S. Martin): Christ’s body in the Mystery is food of the mind, not the belly — not eaten corporally; the same flesh is exhibited spiritually, not corporally.
572: Bernard’s sinewy triple on the Supper: (1) food of the mind = Spiritual food; (2) present and exhibited spiritually, not corporally;

(3) therefore eaten spiritually — eating matches the food’s nature: corporal food for the body, spiritual food received by faith for the faithful soul’s increase of faith and communion with Christ (cf. John 6:56).
573: Later in the age PETER DE BRUIS and Henry the Monk, then PETER WALDO of Lyons with Arnold, preached the true Supper doctrine across Gaul — Lyons and Albi.
Followers called Petrobrusians, Arnoldists, Waldenses, Poor of Lyons, Albigenses — buried under papal flatterers’ calumnies that Our writers (Armachanus among the ablest) repeatedly washed off.
574: Even Pontifical reporters preserve the Waldenses’ genuine reading of the Institution words.

Lombard: some say Christ’s body is not corporally on the altar — ‘This is my Body’ as ‘the Rock was Christ’; body only in the Sacrament/Sign. Rainerius: blessed bread called body in a Figure, as the rock was Christ.
575: Yet they also assert true presence of Christ’s body in the Sacred Supper.
Ancient confession ~1200 (Hoveden fol. 319): We believe he is not saved who does not eat the body of Christ.
576: They do not flee the word Transubstantiation (Rainerius) — but take it spiritually: not in the consecrator’s hand, but in the worthy receiver’s mouth.

Not bread converted into substance there, but the Sacrament exhibitive (not only significative) of the Lord’s body and blood — symbols in the body’s mouth, the thing signified perceived by faith’s taste. Stop before §.XVII.
